Ontology of Fields

What it means for fields to be “real,” the main positions, and key references.

What counts as “physical”?

An entity is physical if it (i) carries energy–momentum, (ii) plays a local causal/explanatory role, and (iii) connects to measurement procedures. For gauge theories, beware that some mathematical features are redundant (gauge freedom).

  • Electromagnetic field: energy density u = (ε₀E² + B²/μ₀)/2, Poynting vector S = (1/μ₀) E × B.
  • Gravitational field (GR): spacetime curvature produces gravitational waves that deliver energy to detectors.
  • QFT view: particles are quanta of underlying fields (e.g., photons, electrons, Higgs).

Main positions

1) Field realism beables

The field (or at least its gauge‑invariant features) is real. Radiation, interference, and field energy support this.

2) Gauge‑redundancy caution

Potentials Aμ are not unique; only invariants like Fμν or loop/holonomy variables are candidates for reality.

3) Structural realism

What’s real is the relational structure: field strengths, holonomies, curvature, stress–energy—not particular gauges.

4) Instrumentalism / EFT

Fields organize phenomena effectively within a scale window; ontology is scale‑dependent (effective field theory).

5) QFT ontology

Quantum fields are operator‑valued distributions; observables are region‑smeared. Particles arise as excitations.

6) Symmetry breaking

Fields can “manifest” via vacuum structure (e.g., Higgs VEV) with real dynamical effects, even without a material medium.

Touchstones & exemplary phenomena

  • Aharonov–Bohm effect: Interference shifts even where E and B vanish, highlighting the physical role of gauge‑invariant loop variables.
  • Gravitational waves: Directly observed by LIGO (2015); ripples of the metric field depositing energy in detectors.
  • Higgs mechanism: Nonzero Higgs field VEV; discovery of the Higgs boson (2012) confirmed the mechanism’s predictions.

Glossary

  • Gauge / gauge freedom: Redundancy in the mathematical description; different gauges represent the same physical state.
  • Gauge‑invariant observable: Quantity unchanged by gauge transformations (e.g., Fμν, Wilson loops, curvature).
  • Holonomy / Wilson loop: Phase/parallel‑transport around a closed loop; captures gauge‑invariant content relevant to Aharonov–Bohm.
  • VEV (vacuum expectation value): Nonzero field value of the vacuum; the Higgs VEV gives masses to W/Z and fermions.
  • Operator‑valued distribution: In QFT, fields are not pointwise functions but linear maps on test functions (smearing).
  • Effective field theory: A field description valid up to a cutoff scale; parameters “run” with energy.
